name: Jiribam Town
description: Jiribam is the headquarters of Jiribam district and the westernmost town of Manipur, serving as the western gateway bordering Assam on the Jiri River.
facts: Known as the Western Gate of Manipur
First railway station in the state is located here
Lies on the bank of the Jiri River near its confluence with the Barak
District formed in 2016 from Imphal East

name: Jiribam Railway Station
description: Jiribam Railway Station is the first railway station in Manipur, connecting the state to the national rail network via Silchar.
facts: Opened in 1903 as part of the Assam Bengal Railway
Station code JRBM under Northeast Frontier Railway
Passenger services to Silchar resumed in 2016
Key entry point for travellers from Assam

name: Ningshingkhul Biodiversity Park
description: Official biodiversity park in Jiribam featuring aquatic and terrestrial plants and animals, along with an Ancestral Heroes Complex.
facts: Listed on official jiribam.nic.in tourist places
About 6 km from Jiribam Railway Station and Bazar
Includes Ancestral Heroes Complex for homage
Focus on local flora and fauna of the region

name: Nongshaba Gate
description: Nongshaba Gate (Western Gate of Manipur) is a symbolic entrance gateway at the western boundary of the state in Jiribam.
facts: Inaugurated in 2021 as the Western Gate of Manipur
Located on the state boundary adjoining Cachar, Assam
Also known as Nongshaba Sanathong
Marks the western entrance for visitors entering Manipur

name: Leishabithol Waterfall
description: Scenic waterfall near Leishabithol village in Jiribam district, offering natural cascades amid forested hills.
facts: Located near Leishabithol census village
Popular local nature spot for day trips from Jiribam
Accessible via local roads with basic trails
Village coordinates approximately 24.7431 N, 93.1565 E

name: Jiri River
description: The Jiri River forms the western boundary of Manipur in the Jiribam area and offers scenic riverbanks for boating and fishing.
facts: Defines the Manipur-Assam border in this region
Near confluence with the Barak River
Supports local agriculture and traditional activities like fishing
Only the eastern bank belongs to Manipur

name: Barak River (Jiribam Section)
description: Section of the Barak River near its confluence with the Jiri River in Jiribam district, known for scenic riverine landscapes.
facts: Major river flowing through the valley south of Jiribam
Confluence with Jiri River near Jirimukh
Important for the geography and ecology of the district
Supports wetlands and agricultural plains

name: Tipaimukh
description: Tipaimukh is the confluence of the Barak and Tuivai rivers at the southern tip of the Vangaitang range in Pherzawl district, a historic trade route point and scenic river junction on the Manipur-Mizoram border.
facts: Mouth of the Tuivai River joining the Barak River
Historic Khongjai trade route to Cachar and Bengal
Barak River makes a U-turn around the Vangaitang range here
Proposed site for the Tipaimukh Dam project
Coordinates approximately 24.235 N, 93.021 E

name: Pherzawl Town
description: Pherzawl is the headquarters of Pherzawl district, a hill town established in 1894 amid lush forests and rivers, serving as the administrative and cultural center for the Hmar-dominated region.
facts: District HQ formed in 2016 from Churachandpur
Founded in 1894 by Bulhmang Infimate
Elevation around 1037 meters
Connected via NH-2 and roads to Imphal and Churachandpur
Official language Hmar

name: Senvawn Village
description: Senvawn (Senvon) is a historic Hmar village in Pherzawl district, known as the birthplace of Christianity in southern Manipur where Welsh missionary Watkin Roberts arrived in 1910.
facts: Birthplace of Christianity in southern Manipur (1910)
Population about 3136 (2011 census)
Located on Senvon Range near Barak and Tuivai rivers
About 22 km from Tipaimukh
Coordinates 24.142 N, 93.048 E

name: Parbung
description: Parbung is a Hmar village and headquarters of Tipaimukh Sub-Division in Pherzawl district, a key administrative and cultural center along NH-2 near the river systems.
facts: HQ of Tipaimukh Sub-Division
Founded in 1897 by Ngamneivung
Population about 2545 (2011)
Heliport under construction
On National Highway 2

name: Barak River (Tipaimukh Section)
description: Scenic section of the Barak River (locally Tuiruong) near Tipaimukh in Pherzawl, where it turns north after the confluence, offering riverine landscapes and historical trade routes.
facts: Major river flowing through southwestern Manipur hills
Makes U-turn at Tipaimukh around Vangaitang range
Forms part of Manipur-Mizoram boundary in places
Source in Senapati district, flows to Bangladesh
Supports local ecology and potential river tourism

name: Luipi Waterfall
description: Luipi Waterfall is a multi-tiered cascade in Pherzawl district, located about 28 km from the district headquarters via NH-2, popular for nature walks and monsoon views.
facts: Listed on official pherzawl.nic.in tourist places
About 28 km from Pherzawl HQ and 163 km from Churachandpur
Fed by perennial hill stream, stronger in monsoon
Accessible via local trails near Joutung area
Coordinates approximate; exact site near NH-2

name: Thanlon
description: Thanlon is the headquarters of Thanlon Sub-Division in Pherzawl district, a hill settlement on NH-2 about 150 km west of Churachandpur, known for its elevated terrain and tribal communities.
facts: HQ of Thanlon Sub-Division
Founded by Simte chief Lumthang
Elevation around 3819 feet
About 150 km from Churachandpur on NH-2
Coordinates approximately 24.283 N, 93.283 E

name: Lungthulien Village
description: Lungthulien is a Hmar village in Pherzawl district near the river confluence areas, featuring traditional lifestyles, cultural sites like stone relics, and scenic hill views.
facts: Hmar village with about 1714 population (2011)
Near Tipaimukh and Parbung areas
Associated with Hmar cultural relics and stones
Coordinates 24.2165 N, 93.086 E
Offers village trails and traditional experiences

name: Tuivai River (Tipaimukh Section)
description: The Tuivai River flows through southern Pherzawl hills and joins the Barak at Tipaimukh, forming scenic valleys and part of the district's riverine landscape and border areas.
facts: Also called Tipai River
Joins Barak River at Tipaimukh confluence
Flows through southern hills of Manipur
Forms sections of Manipur-Mizoram boundary
Supports local ecology and historical routes

name: Hmar Ethnic Cultural Sites
description: Scattered Hmar cultural landmarks in Pherzawl including memorial stones like Sikpui Lung, sacred ponds (Sartuinek, Hringtuinek), and large stone trivets near villages such as Lungthulien, representing pre-Christian traditions and history.
facts: Includes Sikpui Lung memorial and clan unity sites
Sartuinek and Hringtuinek ponds linked to folklore
Lungthu Lien Pathum stone trivets near Lungthulien (~1852)
Primarily in Tipaimukh and Vangai areas
Remote sites requiring local guides and short treks
